cultural.vision_reason: A knife with a native copper leaf-shaped blade, antler/bone handle, and sinew wrapping matches the known style of Copper Inuit knives from Arctic Canada, consistent with the claimed Inuit ethnicity and arms category.

physical.title: knife
physical.summary: Knife constructed with a fine grained antler (?) handle, with a 'V' shaped splice to take the bilaterally flanged finial.The splice and grip are tightly wrapped with a plaited sinew cord, and apparently covered with congealed blood and fat so that it is impossible to see whether the splice is also riveted. At the proximal end the binding is secured through a hole, and at the distal end  is tucked under. The leaf shaped, lanceolate or triangular, native (?) copper blade is set  directly into the handle, and secured with one native (?) copper rivet. The blade has bevelled edges, and no tang.
